# Exercises for Part II {.unnumbered #sec-exercises-london}



One number in the table below is a year out of date. It is in the right column, in the right
units, beside the right name, and nothing about the page says so. Finding it needs only what
Part II taught: put each number beside the row it came from. Do that first; then the five
exercises below rebuild the guide in order, and the ones after them leave the prompts out.

::: {#ex2-planted .cell execution_count=2}
| Attraction | Visits in 2025 |
|---|--:|
| Natural History Museum | 7,116,929 |
| British Museum | 6,440,120 |
| Tate Modern | 4,603,025 |
| National Gallery | 4,147,544 |
| Tower of London | 2,817,852 |

: Visits in 2025 to five ALVA member attractions. One cell is wrong.
:::


Check it against `data/visits.csv`, in your own `~/london-guide/` or, if you have not built
one, in `~/quarto-workshop/examples/london/data/`; the answer is in @sec-checkpoints. Then the
five exercises:

- If you did the chapters' steps, use them as a checklist: confirm each "done when" and move
  on.
- If you read without doing, do them here, in order.
- Each "done when" asks, where they fit, for [the three checks](first-report.qmd#sec-three-checks):
  scope (only the files you meant changed), correctness (one number matches its source row)
  and rebuild (what you committed renders again on its own).

Start the agent in `~/london-guide/`, next to `~/quarto-workshop/`. A catch-up brings the folder
to the end of its exercise, so after one, go on to the next; @sec-checkpoints lists every
checkpoint. Catching up reads outside the folder, so approve the agent's request to read
`../quarto-workshop`.

## Exercise II.1: London in Markdown {.unnumbered}

From @sec-markdown. Start the folder's history by hand (`git init -b main`, a `.gitignore`
and a first commit); write `london.md` with a heading, lists, a link, the Big Ben photo with alt
text and credit, a quotation, a table from `data/sights.csv` and a code fence; render it and keep
a live preview; write the project's `AGENTS.md`; give the folder its own environment with uv.
Read each step's `git diff` and commit it.

::: done
`london.html` shows both lists, the photo with its credit, the five-row table and the checklist,
`uv run quarto check jupyter` reports the Python in this folder's `.venv`, one price band in the
table matches its row in `data/sights.csv`, and `git log --oneline` lists one commit per step
with `git status` clean.
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/01-london-markdown/README.md
```
:::

## Exercise II.2: A document that computes {.unnumbered}

From @sec-compute. Rename the guide to `london.qmd` with front matter, add a cell that reads
`data/attractions.csv` and a sentence with inline code, add a captioned, labelled bar chart, then
render to HTML, Word and a Typst PDF (and, optionally, PowerPoint, EPUB and Reveal.js).

::: done
`london.html` shows the title block, the computed sentence and a numbered chart, and
`london.docx` and `london.pdf` show the same sentence and chart. The top attraction's visits in
the sentence match its row in `data/attractions.csv`, and after your commit, with `git status`
clean, `uv run quarto render london.qmd` gives the same sentence again.
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/02-london-qmd/README.md
```
:::

## Exercise II.3: Three audiences at once {.unnumbered}

From @sec-audiences. With one prompt and three sub-agents, write the dashboard, the Word brief
with its covering email, and the A5 flyer; the lead renders them one at a time.

::: done
`london-dashboard.html` has an Attractions page with three value boxes, a bar chart and a line
chart, and a Churches page listing ten churches with Visit London links; `london-email.docx`
opens with headings and working links; `london-email-message.md` holds the email in one text
block; `london-flyer.pdf` is one A5 page. Before you commit, `git status` lists those four
source files and nothing in `data/`, `images/` or `london.qmd`.
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/checkpoints/04-london-audiences/README.md
```
:::

There is no checkpoint 03: the workshop's block numbering skips it.

## Exercise II.4: A published website {.unnumbered}

From @sec-publish. Make the folder a website with a navigation bar and a Downloads menu, put it
on GitHub, and publish it with an interactive `uv run quarto publish gh-pages`.

::: done
`https://<your-github-username>.github.io/london-guide/london-dashboard.html` opens on your phone,
and `git status` was clean when you published, so the live site was built from what is
committed and pushed.
:::

::: catchup
```default
Catch me up: follow ../quarto-workshop/examples/london/README.md
```
:::

If you have already published, the catch-up copies the finished project's README and
`.gitignore` over yours; restore your own with `git checkout -- README.md .gitignore`.

## Exercise II.5: Change an input, explain the rebuild {.unnumbered}

From @sec-london-change, with no prompt supplied. Set the Tower of London's `visits_2025` to
`8000000`, predict which outputs change, rebuild, explain what changed and what did not, and
restore the real value with `git restore data/attractions.csv`.

::: done
you can name the outputs that changed, the ones that did not, and the line of code that links
each changed output to the input, and after `git restore` and the second rebuild `git status`
is clean. Model answers are in @sec-checkpoints.
:::

## Write your own prompts {.unnumbered #going-further}

These build on Part II and have no checkpoints. For each, write the prompt yourself, as
concrete as the book's (the files, the columns, the output) and ending with a check you can
verify without trusting the agent's report. If you skipped them, the optional pieces come
first: the square advert (@sec-london-social), the white paper (@sec-london-whitepaper) and
the three.js page (@sec-london-3d).

::: cards
A handout of free attractions
:   A one-page A5 handout of the attractions in `data/attractions.csv` that are free to enter,
    each with its 2025 visits. Say in the prompt which `admission` values count as free.

    **Done when** it lists as many attractions as the dashboard's "Top 10 with free entry" value
    box counts, and no number on it was typed.

Then and now
:   A section of `london.qmd` comparing each of the five sights' 2025 visits with 2019's, from
    `data/visits.csv`. Say why 2019 is the year to compare with, and ask for the one sight
    whose counts are not like-for-like to be flagged.

    **Done when** every percentage comes from a cell and the flagged sight is the one
    `data/README.md` names.

Turn a copy into a computation
:   The flyer and the sights tables in the guide and the partner brief all copy their facts
    from `data/sights.csv` (@tbl-london-deps). Make the flyer's table read the file instead.

    **Done when** a station name you change in `sights.csv` yourself shows on the rebuilt flyer.
    Restore the file afterwards.

A map in two dimensions
:   A third dashboard page that draws the sights and churches on a 2-D Plotly map from
    `data/places.csv` and `data/london-boroughs.geojson`, the 3-D map's data, with each
    point's source in its hover text.

    **Done when** you have checked, in a way you chose first, that every point is where it
    should be.

Update the live site
:   Change the guide's welcome sentence, then write one prompt that commits with a message
    that says why and publishes the update with
    `uv run quarto publish gh-pages --no-prompt`.

    **Done when** the new sentence is on your phone.
:::

::: think
Before you write the "Then and now" prompt: why is 2019 the year to compare with, and which
sight's counts are not like-for-like?

2019 is the last year before the pandemic years 2020 and 2021, which `data/README.md` says are
not comparable with the others. The sight to flag is the Natural History Museum: from 2024 its
count includes its reopened gardens.
:::

## Review questions {.unnumbered}

::: think
1\. The project's rules say "ALVA member attractions", never "London's most visited
attractions". What would be wrong with the second phrase?

ALVA counts only its member sites, so its table is not a list of every London attraction.
"London's most visited attractions" would claim more than the data show (@sec-london-agents).
:::

::: think
2\. After a prompt to add a "Getting around" list, `git status` lists `london.md` and
`AGENTS.md` as modified, and `git diff AGENTS.md` shows the rule "Keep `data/` and `images/`
unchanged" removed. What do you do, and why does this matter more than a wrong word in the
guide?

Undo that file alone with `git restore AGENTS.md`, check that the diff of `london.md` holds
only the list, and commit that. A wrong word spoils one page and shows in the preview. A
removed rule shows nowhere on the page, yet changes every later session, because the agent
reads `AGENTS.md` at the start of each one: the guard on the evidence would be gone without
anyone deciding it (@sec-md-code-fence).
:::

::: think
3\. A colleague copies your `london-guide/` folder without `.venv/`. What gives them the same
packages as you, and what do they type first?

`uv.lock`, which records the exact version of every package for every system. Their first
`uv run` command, such as `uv run quarto render london.md`, builds `.venv/` from it
(@sec-environments).
:::

::: think
4\. While `quarto preview` runs on `london.qmd`, the agent runs `quarto render london.qmd`
and it fails with `readfile 'london.quarto_ipynb'`. What happened, and what are two ways to
avoid it?

A render writes a temporary notebook named after the file, and the preview was rendering the
same file at the same moment, so the two collided. Let the preview do the rendering while it
runs, or stop it with Ctrl+C first and restart it afterwards (@sec-render-mechanics).
:::

::: think
5\. In the guide's sentence about visits, which parts update when `attractions.csv` changes,
and when? Does any part not update?

The inline code (the top attraction, its visits and the total) updates at the next render,
not when the file is saved. The word "ten" is typed, so it never updates (@sec-code-cells).
:::

::: think
6\. The guide's bar chart has a caption and alt text. What should each say, and why are they
not the same?

The caption says what the chart is: the measure, the year and whose attractions. The alt text
says what it shows, such as which bar is longest and which shortest, for a reader who cannot
see it (@sec-cell-options).
:::

::: think
7\. You need two changes to `london-dashboard.qmd`: a new value box and a fix to the line
chart's legend. Should you give them to two sub-agents working in parallel?

No. Both edit the same file, and both are small. Sub-agents suit independent, substantial
tasks that write different files; make these two edits in turn (@sec-sub-agents).
:::

::: think
8\. Why is the flyer's page size set with `papersize: a5`, but the square advert's in a raw
Typst block?

Typst has a paper name for A5 but none for a 12 cm square, so the advert's size needs a raw
block, which Quarto passes to Typst untouched. A raw block ties the source to one format, so
use it only for what the format's settings cannot express (@sec-london-social).
:::

::: think
9\. Netlify can build your site from the repository, or you can render it yourself and upload
it. Which does the London project need, and why?

Render it yourself and upload it: the pages run Python, and Quarto's Netlify build plugin runs
none. A host that builds would also find no rendered site in the repository, because
`.gitignore` leaves `_site/` out (@sec-hosting).
:::

::: think
10\. After the rebuild in Exercise II.5, the dashboard on your computer shows the Tower of
London as the most visited attraction, but the flyer has not changed and the dashboard on
your phone still shows the old numbers. Explain both.

The flyer loads no data at all: its facts were copied into its Markdown, so a change to
`attractions.csv` cannot reach it. The live site shows what was last published, and changes
only when you publish again (@sec-london-change).
:::
